title: Evergreen Capital - POC scoping / workload modeling
summary: Initial POC scoping to define success criteria, traffic profile (QPS, concurrency), token distributions, and timeline for a 4-week pilot. Customer wants predictable latency and data residency (VPC/KMS). Agreed to run benchmark with Redwood's perf harness and share traffic samples + pricing. Next: Redwood to send benchmark template and security docs; customer to share top-100 prompts and sample logs.
topics: Workload characterization: QPS, concurrency, input/output token dist
Timeline and next steps for 4-week pilot
action_items: Maya Chen: Share pricing + benchmark spreadsheet and perf harness link (2026-11-11)
Luis Ortega: Provide simple load script and runbook for perf tests (2026-11-13)
Ravi Patel: Share sample traffic profile, top-100 prompts, and current qps/concurrency metrics (2026-11-12)
Jon Kim: Confirm VPC peering network constraints and KMS key availability (2026-11-16)
next_steps: Redwood to send benchmark template, perf harness link, and SOC2 + security docs
Customer to provide sample prompts, token histograms and current infra metrics
Schedule technical deep-dive for perf tuning and quantization options next week
Agree pilot start week of 2026-11-22 for 4 weeks
transcript:
Header: 2026-11-09 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Samantha Price (Evergreen Head of Platform), Ravi Patel (Evergreen Lead ML Eng), Jon Kim (Infra)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, um we'll run through the POC scope, get an understanding of your traffic and agree next steps. Maya here, AE on this account. Luis is our SE for performance.
[00:18] Samantha Price: Great, thanks Maya. Quick context, we are Evergreen Capital, we run a customer support assistant and a transaction summarization pipeline. We're exploring Redwood for inference because current in-house costs and latency are spiking.
[00:30] Ravi Patel: Yeah, to add, our current system is a mix of open models self-hosted and some managed endpoints. We're seeing P95 latency around 700-900ms on average which is too high for chat.
[00:45] Luis Ortega: Ok got it. For the POC we typically benchmark three axes: latency (p50/p95), throughput (QPS and concurrency), and quality/regression vs baseline. Do you have target SLAs?
[00:58] Samantha Price: Target is P95 < 300ms for the chat front-end, and cost per 1k tokens lower than our current infra by at least 20%. Also we need all inference within our VPC or private deployment—data cannot leave our account.
[01:15] Jon Kim: Just to clarify, by VPC you mean peered VPC to Redwood private deployment? There are firewall rules and egress constraints on our side.
[01:23] Maya Chen: Yes — we can do Redwood Private with VPC peering or a dedicated transit arrangement. We'll also support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest. We'll share our security pack.
[01:35] Ravi Patel: Perfect. On traffic profiles — our current production numbers: baseline average QPS ~12, burst to 60 QPS during peak times, concurrency around 30 active sessions. Token distribution: input tokens median ~120, 90th ~420; output tokens median ~40, 90th ~150.
[01:54] Luis Ortega: That's super helpful. For sizing the POC we'll simulate peak: 60 QPS sustained for 10 minutes then back to baseline. For model we recommend testing a 13B open variant and a quantized 8-bit variant to measure tradeoffs. Does that align?
[02:08] Ravi Patel: Yes, we'd like to see the cost/latency tradeoff for quantized variants. Also quality: if quantization drops quality for our prompts we need to see evals.
[02:20] Maya Chen: We'll run a 3-step benchmark: 1) synthetic latency QPS sweep; 2) replay of your top-100 prompts at production token distributions; 3) A/B evaluation for quality regression. We'll provide a spreadsheet where you'll drop in your prompt list and we'll run it against the candidate models.
[02:36] Samantha Price: Timeline — we'd like to kick off the pilot in two weeks and run four weeks. Is that feasible?
[02:43] Luis Ortega: Yes, two weeks is doable. First week we need the sample prompts and token histograms, second week we run baseline perf and iterate. Pilot duration 4 weeks gives enough time for tuning and cost optimization.
[02:58] Jon Kim: Network question — will the perf harness hammer from your cloud or from our VPC? We have strict egress limits.
[03:05] Luis Ortega: We can run the harness inside your VPC (agent mode) or via a peered testing runner. We'll give you a lightweight load script that runs from your infra to Redwood's private endpoint to avoid egress.
[03:18] Ravi Patel: Great. On metrics, besides P95 latency and cost, we also care about 99th and tail latency for heavy requests. For large prompts, the KV cache behavior and prefix caching matter.
[03:30] Maya Chen: Absolutely; part of the deep-dive will cover KV cache warmup and prefix caching behavior. We'll capture per-token breakdown in the traces.
[03:39] Samantha Price: Security — we need SOC 2, audit logs for each request, SSO integration, RBAC and customer-managed KMS. Also data retention policies must be configurable.
[03:52] Maya Chen: Understood. We have SOC2, SAML/SSO, RBAC, request-level audit logs, and you can bring your own KMS. We'll attach our security pack after the call.
[04:01] Jon Kim: Any constraints around model pinning and rollbacks? We need predictable behavior for Canary.
[04:07] Luis Ortega: Yep we support model pinning and canary rollouts, plus automatic fallback to a lower-cost model if latency spikes. We'll explain routing policies in the op docs.
[04:17] Ravi Patel: For the benchmark I want to see tokenized histograms per prompt, p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput at concurrency 1, 8, 16, 32, and the cost per 1k tokens for each model variant.
[04:30] Maya Chen: Great checklist. We'll include those columns in the spreadsheet. We'll also show suggestions for batching and quantization to hit cost targets.
[04:39] Samantha Price: On success criteria, let's write it down: 1) P95 chat latency < 300ms, 2) model quality within 2% of current baseline on our eval set, 3) total monthly inference cost reduction >= 20% at expected load, 4) security controls in place (VPC, KMS, audit logs).
[04:57] Maya Chen: Sounds good — we can sign off on those as POC success metrics.
[05:03] Luis Ortega: Few gotchas: tokenization differences between model families can change cost, so we'll normalize by token counts in the report. Also quantized models may have slightly different output formatting; we'll include automated eval diffs.
[05:17] Samantha Price: Ok, logistics — who owns the test data upload?
[05:21] Ravi Patel: We'll upload anonymized prompts and a small sample of historical logs. Need to confirm retention windows.
[05:27] Maya Chen: We'll accept uploads via a secure S3 presigned flow into the private environment; retention configurable.
[05:33] Jon Kim: Network — I'll follow up with firewall egress rules doc.
[05:37] Maya Chen: Great, action items captured. Any final questions?
[05:42] Samantha Price: No, this is good. Please send the security pack and the benchmark template.
[05:47] Maya Chen: Will do. We'll target to send those by 2026-11-11 and kick off the run week of 2026-11-22.
[05:54] Ravi Patel: One last note — can you include a quick estimate of Dedicated vs Private pricing for the expected load? We might prefer Dedicated if latency is easier to guarantee.
[06:03] Maya Chen: Yes we'll include both line items in the pricing sheet and note SLO differences.
[06:09] Luis Ortega: I'll also prepare a short doc on quantization tradeoffs and per-model perf expectations.
[06:15] Samantha Price: Perfect, thanks everyone.
[06:18] Maya Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the materials and a calendar invite for the tech deep-dive.

End of call.
questions: Can Redwood run perf harness inside our VPC to avoid egress?
What's the expected latency improvement with 8-bit quantized variants?
How are request-level audit logs surfaced and for how long are they retained?
